comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C59-C63. Both evaluations support that AARS2 overexpression does not affect cardiomyocyte proliferation, vessel density, or hypertrophy, establishing that protective effects work through alternative mechanisms.

Strong agreement on claims C78-C84 regarding PKM2 regulation. Both evaluations support that Ribo-Seq demonstrates increased PKM2 translation with AARS2 overexpression and selective PKM2 (not PKM1) regulation.
Strong agreement on claims C93-C99. Both evaluations support the pharmacological rescue experiments showing TEPP-46 reverses AARS2 deficiency phenotypes, validating the PKM2-mediated mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C43-C48. Both evaluations support the mechanistic findings of increased apoptosis and impaired metabolism in AARS2 knockout models using TUNEL staining, apoptotic markers, and Seahorse assays.

Strong agreement on claims C64-C70. Both evaluations support the cardioprotective effects of AARS2 overexpression, including reduced apoptosis, decreased mtROS, and lower LDH release in both in vivo and in vitro models.

Strong agreement on claims C71-C76 regarding metabolic shift. Both evaluations support mass spectrometry and Seahorse data demonstrating AARS2 overexpression shifts metabolism from OXPHOS toward glycolysis. OpenEval notes C77 is speculative, but peer review does not address this claim.

Strong agreement on claims C100-C126 (overlapping C100, C102, C104, C111, C125, C126). Both evaluations support the overarching conclusion that AARS2 represents a novel cardioprotective pathway via PKM2-mediated metabolic regulation.

Strong agreement on claims C36-C42. Both evaluations support the cardiomyopathy phenotype in AARS2 knockout mice with reduced cardiac function, mortality, hypertrophy, and fibrosis. Peer review also includes C120 (summary claim) not in OpenEval R2.

Strong agreement on claims C52-C58. Both evaluations support that AARS2 overexpression provides cardioprotection post-MI with improved echocardiographic parameters and reduced fibrosis. Peer review also includes C121 (summary claim).

Agreement on claims C85-C88, C92 regarding mechanism. Both evaluations support that AARS2 regulates PKM2 oligomeric forms through alanine-mediated translational/metabolic mechanisms rather than direct interaction. Peer review also includes C105, C106, C109.

Agreement on claims C89-C91. Both evaluations support that AARS2 does not directly interact with PKM2 (co-IP negative) and does not regulate PKM2 transcriptionally (qRT-PCR unchanged), establishing translational regulation.

Agreement on claims C49-C51. Both evaluations support successful generation of cardiomyocyte-specific AARS2 overexpression model with heart-specific expression confirmed by Western blot and immunofluorescence.

Agreement on claims C33-C35. Both evaluations support successful cardiomyocyte-specific AARS2 knockout with reduced AARS2 in hearts but not other tissues. Peer review groups these with broader phenotype claims (C36-C42, C120).

Agreement on claims C113-C114 regarding metabolic shift confirmation. Both evaluations support Seahorse data showing increased glycolytic capacity. OpenEval R14 also includes mechanistic integration (C115-C117) partially covered in peer R5 and R11.
Agreement on claim C123. Both evaluations support Ribo-Seq evidence for PKM2 regulation. OpenEval R13 is a summary result covering multiple findings (C120-C124) distributed across peer reviews.
Agreement on claim C124. Both evaluations support pharmacological validation with TEPP-46. OpenEval R13 summarizes main findings while peer R10 provides detailed evaluation of rescue experiments.
Agreement on claim C120. Both evaluations support loss-of-function phenotype summary. OpenEval R13 is a comprehensive summary result while peer R1 focuses on knockout phenotype details.
Agreement on claim C121. Both evaluations support gain-of-function protection summary. OpenEval R13 provides comprehensive summary while peer R3 details overexpression protective effects.
Agreement on claim C122. Both evaluations support mechanistic basis involving metabolic shift and reduced ROS. OpenEval R13 is summary while peer R5 provides detailed protective mechanism evaluation.

Agreement on claim C115. Both evaluations support reduced mtROS as part of protective mechanism. OpenEval R14 integrates metabolic and protective mechanisms while peer R5 focuses on cardioprotective effects.
Agreement on claim C117. Both evaluations support PKM2-mediated metabolic adaptation model. OpenEval R14 provides mechanistic integration while peer R11 supports overarching conclusions.

Agreement on claim C103. Both evaluations support that loss-of-function causes metabolic impairment and cell death. OpenEval R12 synthesizes overall findings while peer R2 evaluates knockout mechanisms.
Agreement on claim C109. Both evaluations support that mechanism involves PKM2 regulation. OpenEval R12 provides comprehensive synthesis while peer R8 focuses on alanine-PKM2 mechanism.

OpenEval R15 evaluates background claims C1-C6 (CVD epidemiology, MI etiology, cardiomyocyte limitations) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than background literature.

OpenEval R16 evaluates background claims C7-C14 (ischemic injury mechanisms, ATP depletion, ROS toxicity) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers did not assess background literature claims.

OpenEval R17 evaluates background claims C15-C21 (mt-AARSs function, AARS2 structure, disease associations) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers focused on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval R18 evaluates background claims C22-C28 (pyruvate kinase biology, isoforms, tissue distribution) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers did not assess background literature.

OpenEval R19 evaluates claims C29-C30 (authors' previous work and unpublished observations) as supported context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these claims inform study rationale.

OpenEval R20 evaluates claims C101-C118 (contextual literature on AARS2 mutations, PKM2 role, TEPP-46 mechanism) as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers did not separately assess literature context claims.

OpenEval R21 identifies claims C32, C77, C119 as speculative beyond experimental data (AARS2 involvement inference, protective mechanism hypothesis, chronic glycolysis uncertainty). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not explicitly flag these speculative elements.
